title: UnitedHealth Says Chart Review Time Falls 33% With AI Usage
key_facts: On UnitedHealth Group's third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026, chief executive Steve Hemsley described a company-wide push to build 'agentic infrastructure'.
AI-enabled chart summarization has been expanded to more than 40% of UnitedHealth's employed clinicians and has cut chart review time by 33%.
AI-enabled information gathering and research have reduced appeal cycle times by 26%, which Hemsley said will likely accelerate next year.
For Medicare Advantage open enrolment the insurer is introducing AI-powered plan recommendations based on a member's care history and local options.
UnitedHealth says it is on pace to reduce prior authorization volumes by 30%.
Third-quarter revenue was $112.7 billion (down slightly from $113.2 billion a year earlier); earnings from operations were $6.6 billion against $4.3 billion.
PYMNTS notes the Doctors Not AI Act, which would bar an automated system from having the final say on whether an insurer approves a claim; sponsor Rep. Greg Landsman (D-Ohio) is quoted.
quote_evidence: “Across the businesses, AI-enabled capabilities are beginning to help clinicians spend more time with patients,” Hemsley said.

why_it_matters_hint: The largest US insurer-and-care group says AI is already cutting paperwork time for its clinicians, while lawmakers want limits on AI in claim decisions.
notes: Full PYMNTS text read. The article spells the chief executive 'Hemsley' (and once 'Hemsely'); 'Steve Hemsley' as printed. All AI percentages are company claims made on the call. The article does not say what the appeals are about, so the entry says only 'appeal cycles'.
